blocks.text: Skin, the outermost layer of the body, gives the first defence against microbes. Its epidermis is 10 to 30 cells thick. The outer layer, the stratum corneum, is continuously damaged and shed; new cells formed deep in the epidermis move up to replace them, and these cells make keratin, a protein that makes the skin tough and impenetrable to microbes.

blocks.alt: A section of skin. At the top a thin stratum corneum of dead cells, then the epidermis of rounded cells, then a thick dermis containing a hair with its follicle, an oil gland beside the hair, a coiled sweat gland with its duct, and red and blue blood vessels, and a fat layer at the bottom.
blocks.caption: Layers of the skin (original diagram after Figure 21.2).
blocks.long_description: Skin is the first barrier against microbes. Its epidermis is 10 to 30 cells thick; the outer stratum corneum is continuously worn and shed and replaced by cells moving up from the deep epidermis, and these cells make keratin, which makes the skin tough and impenetrable. Oil and sweat glands lower the surface pH to 3-5, acid enough to inhibit many microbes, and sweat contains lysozyme, which digests the cell walls of many bacteria.

blocks.text: Skin also defends with chemicals: oil and sweat glands lower the surface pH to 3-5, acid enough to inhibit the growth of many microbes, and sweat contains the enzyme lysozyme, which attacks and digests the cell walls of many bacteria.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: Skin is the largest organ of the vertebrate body; in an adult human it is about 15% of the total weight. According to the book, one square centimetre of human skin has 200 nerve endings, 10 hairs and muscles, 100 sweat glands, 15 oil glands, 3 blood vessels, 12 heat receptors, 2 cold receptors and 25 pressure receptors.

blocks.prompt: Give two ways the skin keeps microbes out.
blocks.explanation: Any two: a tough keratin layer that is constantly shed; an acidic surface (pH 3-5) from oil and sweat; lysozyme in sweat that digests bacterial walls.

items: Epidermis 10-30 cells; shed stratum corneum; keratin makes skin tough.
Acid surface (pH 3-5) and lysozyme in sweat.
